title: Tom's Baby — gold vein specimen recovered from Gold Flake Mine
label: Tom's Baby gold specimen, found at Gold Flake Mine in 1887; photographed in a museum in 2012 — NOT the mine exterior.
sourceTitle: Gold vein stockwork in limonite (Gold Flake Vein, Farncomb Hill, near Breckenridge, Colorado, USA) 12 (16891788938).jpg
sourceNote: Exact-site historical artifact: the celebrated 'Tom's Baby' high-grade gold/limonite specimen was recovered from the Gold Flake Mine on Farncomb Hill on 23 July 1887. This is a modern photograph of the specimen on display at Denver Museum of Nature & Science, not a photograph of the mine, shaft, surface works, or original 1887 discovery. Supplemental image only; the specimen should not be portrayed as a mine exterior or a site-condition photograph. Unmodified original image.
identityEvidence: The original Wikimedia Commons file description identifies the pictured specimen as 'Tom's Baby' and gives its origin as the Gold Flake Vein, 90 feet below surface in the Gold Flake Mine, Ware-Carpenter Claims, Farncomb Hill. Independent Denver Public Library Colorado chronology (https://history.denverlibrary.org/sites/history/files/ColoradoChronology2020.pdf) confirms a 156-ounce gold specimen from the Gold-Flake Mine on 23 July 1887; Town of Breckenridge historical memo also identifies Gold Flake Mine as its origin. Exact provenance is to the mine's ore specimen, NOT the mine structure.
